knowledge_point.title: Differentiating an Exponential Function with a Nonlinear Exponent

question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we express $f(x)$ as the composite function

$$
f={e}^{u},\,u=-{x}^{6}.
$$

Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}u}={e}^{u},\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-6{x}^{5}.
$$

We now apply the chain rule and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & ={e}^{u}\cdot (-6{x}^{5}) \\  & =-6{x}^{5}{e}^{u} \\  & =-6{x}^{5}{e}^{-{x}^{6}}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we express $y$ as the composite function

$$
y={e}^{u},\,u=-4{x}^{6}-2x.
$$

Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}={e}^{u},\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-24{x}^{5}-2.
$$

We now apply the chain rule and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & ={e}^{u}\cdot (-24{x}^{5}-2) \\  & =(-24{x}^{5}-2){e}^{u} \\  & =(-24{x}^{5}-2){e}^{-4{x}^{6}-2x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the slope $m$ of the tangent to the curve at $x=-1$, we have to evaluate $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}m={\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=-1} & ={((-24{x}^{5}-2){e}^{-4{x}^{6}-2x})|}_{x=-1} \\  & =(-24(-1)^{5}-2){e}^{-4(-1)^{6}-2(-1)} \\  & =22{e}^{-2} \\  & =22{e}^{-2}\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we express $y$ as the composite function

$$
y=e^{u},\,u={x}^{3}-{x}^{2}+4.
$$

Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}=e^{u},\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=3{x}^{2}-2x.
$$

We now apply the chain rule and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\ & =e^{u}\cdot (3{x}^{2}-2x) \\ & =(3{x}^{2}-2x)e^{u} \\ & =\left(3 x^{2} - 2 x\right) e^{x^{3} - x^{2} + 4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the slope $m$ of the tangent to the curve at $x=-2$, we have to evaluate $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}m=\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|_{x=-2} & =(3{x}^{2}-2x)e^{{x}^{3}-{x}^{2}+4}|_{x=-2} \\ & =(3(-2)^{2}-2(-2))e^{(-2)^{3}-(-2)^{2}+4} \\ & =16\cdot e^{-8} \\ & =\frac{16}{e^{8}}.\end{aligned}
$$
